steps.stem: The speaker's heavy reliance on ____ gives his lecture the character of ____ ; the audience was therefore surprised when, amid the lecture's ____ style, he repeatedly paused to ____ .
choices: detailed statistical tables / a technical report / dry and impersonal / tell jokes about his own childhood
precise legal terminology / an official document / formal / quote the exact wording of the relevant laws
colorful personal anecdotes / a dry academic paper / lively and humorous / share amusing stories
simple words and short sentences / a talk for young children / playful / ask the audience easy questions
explanation: Only personal jokes clash with a dry, impersonal style, so only (1) justifies "surprised". In (2) and (4) the last part fits the style, so nothing is surprising; in (3) anecdotes cannot make a lecture a dry academic paper.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Critics of the grading reform introduced by Principal Harel argue that since the reform took effect, the time teachers spend checking each student's written assignment ____ . Harel ____ that checking an assignment now takes longer than it did in the past, ____ the extra time is evidence of a genuine improvement in teaching, and that ____ .
choices: has decreased / accepts / but maintains that / the teachers' workload has become considerably lighter
has increased considerably / does not dispute / but maintains that, far from being a flaw, / students now receive far more detailed comments on their work
has increased / freely admits / but, in contrast to his critics, holds that / checking an assignment is now quicker than it once was
has decreased / is convinced / but adds in the same breath that / the checking process has become far too slow
explanation: Harel concedes the critics' point (more time) and turns it into an advantage, and detailed comments support that view. (1) and (3) contradict the admission that checking takes longer; (4) calls the change an improvement and "far too slow" at once.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.title: Sentence completion - connectors and method
steps.intro: The link between the parts of the sentence decides the answer. Know the connectors by what they do.

tables.title: Connectors by function
head: Link
English connectors
rows: but · however · although · even though · despite · nevertheless · yet · whereas · unlike
admittedly … but · does not deny … but · even if · even so
because · since · owing to · therefore · thus · for this reason · so
and · moreover · and even · likewise · not only … but also
for example · such as · that is · a colon ( : ) · a dash ( - )
if · unless · only if · provided that
had … / were … (= if) · had it not been for · were it not for · but for (= if not)

tables.title: The method
head: Step
What to do
rows: Shrink the sentence to its skeleton: cross out noise, rewrite hard parts briefly
Read with an option in place - never with holes
Plug in by similar beginnings; predict how the sentence should go on
Parts contradict each other → eliminate (the sentence’s logic, not world knowledge)
It fits → mark it and move on; don’t check the rest

tips: Hypothetical: what really happened is the reverse of what is written.
Had it not been for X, Y would… → because of X, not Y.
A hunch may choose which option to try first - never mark without checking.

steps.stem: ____ found that the inspector's report, according to which the old building is safe, was ____ , the residents would not have been ____ their apartments.
choices: Had the engineer / reliable / allowed to stay in
Had the engineer not / inaccurate / allowed to stay in
Had the engineer / inaccurate / ordered to leave
Had the engineer not / inaccurate / ordered to leave
explanation: What really happened is the reverse of what is written: the engineer found the "safe" report inaccurate, so the residents were ordered to leave. (2) makes the residents stay although the report was rejected; (1) and (3) use a positive condition that gives the opposite result.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: ____ that Tamar generally refuses to lend her tools, ____ when she ____ her new drill.
choices: Had I known / I would have been hurt / refused to lend me
Had I not known / I would have been hurt / offered to lend me
Had I not known / I would not have been surprised / offered to lend me
Had I known / I would not have been surprised / agreed to lend me
explanation: Because I knew that Tamar does not lend her tools, I was surprised when she offered me her drill. In (1) knowing would prevent the hurt; in (2) no one is hurt by an offer; in (4) knowing is exactly what would cause the surprise.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In an address she gave at a national forestry conference, Dr. Halevi argued that ____ the use of grazing goats to clear undergrowth in forests, ____ this practice. She explained that goat grazing makes it possible to reduce the use of heavy machinery for clearing, ____ young saplings that are important for the renewal of the forest ____ .
choices: in view of the success achieved by / steps should be taken to extend / which admittedly also damages / but the harm the machines cause is far less than the harm the goats cause to those same saplings
despite the failure of / it is nonetheless right to extend / and although the goats have occasionally damaged / this casts serious doubt on the practice's seemingly impressive results
even if one disregards the failure of / there are many reasons to oppose / which is liable to damage / in addition to the harm it causes to the soil

despite the success achieved by / limits should be placed on / and even to lower the cost of maintaining the forest; but since the goats also eat / there are areas in which the harm they cause outweighs their benefit
explanation: Only (4) explains why a successful method should still be limited: the goats also eat the saplings. (1) ends by arguing against the goats while calling to extend their use; (3) praises goats in the justification while claiming there are reasons to oppose them.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: When determining whether two unsigned paintings were made by the same artist, great weight should be given to similarity in brushwork technique, and only secondary weight to similarity in subject matter - a similarity that may simply reflect the fashion of the period. Thus, for example, the fact that both paintings depict a harbor at sunset does suggest a connection between them, but ____ .
choices: what would establish this connection is similarity in the way the paint is applied, as for example in the short, thick strokes used to render the water in both works
the fact that the brushwork in the two paintings is similar shows that this similarity is merely a matter of chance
what truly indicates a common artist is precisely the similarity in subject, such as the choice of boats and gulls
to determine this one must first establish which of the two paintings was completed earlier
explanation: The sentence applies the stated rule: subject similarity only hints, brushwork decides. (3) reverses the weighting; (2) contradicts the rule; (4) raises an irrelevant question of priority.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: What makes a novel deserving of a literary prize? ____ considerable disagreement among the judging panels of different prizes, ____ to honor a novel that another panel ____ . Nevertheless, when judges are asked to explain their choices, ____ : the originality of the plot, the quality of the writing, and the book's relevance to its time.
choices: There is clearly / since it often happens that a panel decides / passed over / they all cite the same criteria
We might expect to find / but in practice it is not unusual for a panel to agree / dismissed / each of them gives a different explanation
There appears to be no / since it rarely happens that a panel refuses / has already honored / the same criteria are mentioned again and again
Only rarely is there / and therefore it is not unusual for a panel to choose / passed over / they offer a variety of explanations
explanation: "Nevertheless" requires a contrast between real disagreement and shared criteria, which only (1) supplies. (3) denies the disagreement, so there is nothing to contrast; (2) and (4) end with varied explanations, which does not contrast with disagreement.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: If ____ that the old bridge was unsafe ____ you to drive more slowly across it, then all the more so ____ would not have made you drive across it ____ .
choices: an unconfirmed rumor / made / an official warning from the city engineer / more slowly
the official warning from the city engineer / made / a rumor / faster
an unconfirmed rumor / did not make / an official warning from the city engineer / more slowly
the official warning from the city engineer / did not make / an unconfirmed rumor / more slowly
explanation: "All the more so" moves from the stronger case to the weaker one: if even an official warning did not slow you down, a rumor surely would not. (3) runs the inference from the weak case to the strong one.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: A consumer advocate secretly recorded conversations with the sales staff of a car dealership, and thereby revealed that the dealership was systematically misleading buyers about the terms of its warranty. Some condemned the secret recording, ____ : in my opinion, ____ revealing the deception served the public interest, the argument that in this case the result excused the method ____ , since the advocate ____ simply by reading the warranty documents that the dealership hands to every buyer.
choices: but I do not share their view / even though / holds / could not have uncovered the deception
and I share their view / even though / does not hold / could have uncovered the deception
and I share their view / although / does not hold / could not have uncovered the deception
but I do not share their view / since / holds / could have uncovered the deception
explanation: The recording was unnecessary because the documents already revealed the deception, so the method is not excused despite the public benefit. In (4) the method was unnecessary, yet the writer claims it was justified; (3) gives a reason that supports the recording while rejecting it.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: ____ the new coach's training methods ____ last season, the club's veteran players regard her instructions for the coming season ____ .
choices: owing to the fact that / produced the team's worst results in years / with great respect
although / led the team to the championship / with suspicion
despite the fact that / led the team to the championship / with complete trust
even though / produced the team's worst results in years / skeptically
explanation: Only (2) sets a real contrast: her methods succeeded, yet the players are suspicious. In (3) and (4) the attitude follows naturally from the results, so the concessive connector does not fit; in (1) the cause does not lead to the result.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The photographer Anna Lindqvist has often stated that ____ portray a place truthfully ____ lived there for at least a year. This belief ____ why she ____ the invitation to photograph the research stations in the Arctic, where she has never lived.
choices: a photographer cannot / unless they have / therefore does not help explain / turned down
a photographer can / only if they have not / may therefore explain / declined
a photographer can / only if they have not / therefore does not help explain / did not decline
a photographer cannot / unless they have / may therefore explain / declined
explanation: Her belief requires having lived in a place, so it explains why she declined to photograph a place she never lived in. (1) has the right belief and decision but denies the obvious explanation; (2) and (3) state an absurd belief.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In a study, participants spent six weeks working in a very quiet environment. They were then asked to rate the loudness of recorded sounds, and they rated them as louder than did people who had worked in an ordinary office. The researchers therefore hypothesized that the quiet period had made the participants more sensitive to sound, so that now ____ it turned out that in the weeks after the study ended the participants tended to set the volume on their televisions and phones higher than they had before the study.
choices: they would need a higher volume in order to hear comfortably. And indeed,
a lower volume would be enough for them to hear comfortably. And indeed,
they would need a higher volume in order to hear comfortably. However, to their surprise,
a lower volume would be enough for them to hear comfortably. However, to their surprise,
explanation: Greater sensitivity predicts that a lower volume would suffice; raising the volume contradicts this prediction, so "to their surprise" is required. (1) and (3) reverse what greater sensitivity implies.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Does relying on navigation apps harm drivers' sense of direction? Does the ease of finding a route with an app keep drivers from developing the ability to find their way on their own? ____ . But since, as far as we know, this is not the case, then even if navigation apps become more accurate and more widespread, drivers' sense of direction will not be harmed, and may even improve as a result.
choices: If drivers could develop a good sense of direction without ever having to find their way on their own, relying on the apps would do no harm at all
It would make sense to encourage the use of these apps if heavy traffic were the main obstacle to developing drivers' sense of direction
If a navigation app could replace the driver's need to build a mental picture of the route, that would weaken drivers' sense of direction
There is some logic in the claim that drivers' sense of direction will not keep developing without aids that overcome the limits of human memory
explanation: The conclusion (no harm) follows only if "this is not the case" denies a condition for harm, as in (3). Denying (1)'s condition would imply harm; (2) and (4) are not conditions whose denial leads to the conclusion.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: A school principal wrote: "What is 'restorative discipline'? It is an approach that rethinks several basic assumptions of school discipline: instead of the usual focus on punishing the offender, it seeks to repair the harm done, to rebuild trust and to strengthen shared responsibility - principles whose core is the dignity and well-being of every member of the school community, including, of course, the offender. ____ : it insists that every student who has caused harm face those they have hurt and take concrete, demanding steps to make amends."
choices: However, in practice its responses to specific incidents often fail to reflect these principles
That said, this is not a lenient approach that avoids confrontation and settles for a quick apology. Quite the opposite
Nevertheless, many of its features show that it cares about the welfare of the offender too
However, in practice there is no real difference between it and ordinary school discipline, either in its guiding principles or in the actions that follow from them
explanation: The sentence after the colon shows the approach is demanding, which illustrates (2). (3) repeats what was already said about the offender, so "Nevertheless" has nothing to contrast with; (1) and (4) are not illustrated by the colon sentence.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Daniel, a theater director, is convinced that rehearsals marked by ____ lead to performances that ____ . He therefore hopes that he is ____ in his feeling that the cast ____ the staging he has planned for the new play, which they will rehearse for the first time tomorrow.
choices: complete harmony / are lifeless and predictable / wrong / are unhappy with
heated arguments / nobody enjoys / right / are unhappy with
heated arguments / are fresh and daring / wrong / are happy with
complete harmony / fail to reach their full potential / right / are happy with
explanation: Daniel thinks disagreement produces good performances, so he hopes the cast is not in fact content with his staging. In every other option his hope would lead to the result he considers bad.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The Coastal Research Institute's ____ report on the state of the coral reefs along the southern coast ____ . "____ ," say ____ .
choices: alarming / left the Ministry of Tourism unmoved / Only if funding is found quickly / officials in the minister's office, "will the reefs be saved from destruction"
encouraging / has brought smiles to the faces of divers / This is certainly good news / the latter, "we have managed to destroy large parts of the reefs"
alarming / did not leave the authorities unmoved / There is hope / its authors, "that we will not be able to save large parts of the reefs"
encouraging / is not enough to reassure marine biologists / More funding is needed / the latter, "or else large parts of the reefs will be lost"
explanation: Only (4) is consistent throughout: good news, yet not enough, so the biologists demand more funds. In (1) a ministry that is unmoved urges urgent funding; (2) and (3) end with quotes that contradict their opening.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Dr. Noa Ravid: "Geology teaches that understanding a landscape as it looks today depends on understanding the forces that shaped it over millions of years, and it may be argued that the founding years of an organization parallel those forces, since in both cases the early period reveals the pressures that determined the basic structure before later layers covered them. Accordingly, ____ ."
choices: the pressures at work in organizations are probably the same forces at work in shaping landscapes
organizations, like landscapes, are gradually covered over by later layers
understanding an organization's founding years is a condition for understanding the organization as it is today
understanding a landscape requires examining the layers that covered it in later periods
explanation: The analogy transfers the geological rule (present depends on formative past) to organizations, as in (3). (1) equates the two domains literally; (2) restates a side detail; (4) stays in geology and reverses the rule.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: A study of employees at a large factory found that workers with few friends at work were more likely to leave, especially in years in which the company cut wages: in years of wage cuts, the likelihood that a worker with close friendships at work would still be with the company at the end of the year was ____ that of a worker with few such friendships, and in years without cuts it was ____ .
choices: four times as high as / twice as high
twice as high as / four times as high
half as high as / a quarter as high
a quarter as high as / half as high
explanation: Workers with friends stay more, and the gap is largest in wage-cut years, so the ratio must be higher then. (2) puts the larger gap in the wrong years; (3) and (4) make friendless workers more likely to stay.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The architect Maya Katz asked a colleague to look over an objection ____ her building plan, and he told her that the arguments raised in the objection ____ , and moreover that several expert opinions could be cited in their support. "Even so," he added, "don't give up: in my experience, objections of this kind ____ , so it is still ____ that this one will be dismissed."
choices: submitted in support of / are sound / are dismissed only very rarely / hardly conceivable
filed against / are not groundless / are upheld in most cases / not reasonable
filed against / are persuasive at first sight / are upheld in only a few cases / quite possible
submitted in support of / have no basis in the regulations / are upheld fairly often / not certain
explanation: "Even so ... don't give up" needs strong arguments against her plan and yet a real chance of dismissal. (2) offers no hope; (1) and (4) make the objection support her plan, so there is nothing to hope for.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Unlike Yael, Omer thinks that ____ approve the plan to close the neighborhood's old public library. In his view, Yael holds on to her position ____ aware that the library ____ .
choices: it is right to / even though she is / serves hundreds of elderly residents who have no other access to books
there is no reason not to / even though she is not / serves hundreds of elderly residents who have no other access to books
there is no need to / since she is not / costs the city a great deal to maintain and is rarely used
it would be wrong to / even though she is / serves hundreds of elderly residents who have no other access to books
explanation: Omer opposes closing, so Yael supports it despite knowing the library serves many residents. In (1) Yael opposes closing "even though" she knows a fact that supports her; in (3) her ignorance of the costs would not explain supporting closure.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The historian Dr. Weiss used to argue that old buildings that have lost their original purpose ____ torn down. ____ his daughter, ____ on this question, decided ____ the abandoned railway station, which the town council had voted to demolish.
choices: should rightly be / It is therefore easy to understand why / who adopted his view / to lead the campaign to save
should not be / It is surprising that / who disagreed with him / nevertheless to lead the campaign to save
should not be / It is therefore easy to understand why / although she rejected his view / not even to sign the petition to save
should rightly be / It is therefore astonishing that / who shared his view / not even to sign the petition to save
explanation: She disagrees with preserving old buildings yet leads the campaign to save one: surprising, as (2) says. In (1) and (4) her action contradicts or matches the shared view with the wrong reaction; in (3) her behavior follows from her rejection, not "therefore" from his view.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem:
Dr. Amsalem: "In a country's core constitutional principles only minor amendments can be made over the years, and far-reaching reforms are possible only in ordinary legislation."
Dr. Hart: "I disagree with you. ____ ."
choices: Far-reaching reforms can be made in a country's core constitutional principles as well
Minor amendments can be made in ordinary legislation as well
In ordinary legislation far-reaching reforms can be made
Over the years every country makes both minor amendments and far-reaching reforms in its laws
explanation: Only (1) contradicts Amsalem's claim. (3) repeats it; (2) and (4) are compatible with it.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: Gil claims that ____ the injury to his ankle, he ____ the marathon in under four hours. His coach ____ this claim, and as evidence points out that in each of Gil's three previous marathons he took more than four and a half hours, ____ .
choices: had it not been for / could have finished / agrees with / even though he was fully fit in all of them
even without / would not have finished / agrees with / even though he was fully fit in all of them
had he not recovered from / would not have finished / disagrees with / since he was injured in all of them
even had he not recovered from / would have finished / agrees with / since he was injured in all of them
explanation: Gil says the injury made no difference; the coach agrees because Gil was slow even when fit. In (1) and (4) the evidence contradicts the claim the coach agrees with; in (3) the evidence supports the claim the coach disputes.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The violin solo was performed at a level that ____ the level expected of soloists in the country's leading orchestras. ____ amazed to learn that the performer was ____ a twelve-year-old pupil, ____ a seasoned professional.
choices: falls far short of / I was therefore / none other than / from whom one cannot expect playing like that of
is not below / I was therefore / none other than / and not
is in no way below / I was therefore not / none other than / and not
falls far short of / I was therefore not / not / but rather
explanation: Professional-level playing by a child is amazing, as (2) says. (3) says the writer was not amazed; in (1) and (4) weak playing gives no reason for the reaction described.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The Arbel bakery's bread ____ the bread of the Golan bakery, ____ surprising that it sells ____ than Golan's bread, since Golan's prices are lower. ____ .
choices: is admittedly less tasty than / but it is / more / For this reason Arbel is now looking for ways to cut its prices
is admittedly tastier than / but it is nevertheless / more / After all, it is well known that shoppers care far more about taste than about price
is in no way inferior in taste to / and even so it is not / less / For this reason Arbel is now looking for ways to cut its prices
is not as tasty as / and it is nevertheless / less / After all, it is well known that shoppers care far more about taste than about price
explanation: Equal taste plus higher price explains lower sales, so Arbel works on price. In (2) and (4) the final sentence removes the surprise that was just claimed; in (1) a bakery that sells more has no reason to cut prices.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In her review of the new album by the singer Tom Avrahami, the music critic wrote: "Songs about lost love ____ a formula for a dull album, ____ the singer Rina Mor, ____ , Avrahami ____ to give these songs genuine depth and freshness."
choices: are not necessarily / but unlike / who wrote such songs brilliantly / does not manage
are / and indeed, like / who wrote such songs in a clichéd and shallow way / manages admirably
are not necessarily / and indeed, like / who wrote such songs brilliantly / does not manage
are / but unlike / who wrote such songs in a clichéd and shallow way / does not manage
explanation: The theme can succeed (Mor proved it), but Avrahami fails, so "unlike" is right. (3) says "like" for opposite results; (4) says "unlike" for the same result; (2) contradicts "and indeed".
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: A person who lives in a city today would hardly recognize the same city as it looked two hundred years ago. From this one might conclude that at some point its residents must have felt that they had suddenly been moved to a strange place. After all, ____ . However, sweeping historical transformations are very often a series of small changes that go unnoticed.
choices: the street names in many cities have hardly changed over the centuries
a river carves a canyon slowly, but in the end the whole landscape is transformed
many migrations in history were driven by residents' wish to leave their home cities
a person who fell asleep and woke to find every building on their street replaced would feel completely lost
explanation: "After all" must support the tempting conclusion with an example of sudden change causing disorientation, as in (4). (2) illustrates gradual change, which belongs to the "However" sentence; (1) and (3) are irrelevant.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: The prices of solar panels have been falling ____ , ____ a system that only wealthy households could afford a decade ago can today ____ .
choices: so steeply / that / be installed by many families of modest means
only slightly / and therefore / be found on the roof of almost every home
at a dizzying rate / with the result that / be seen as an unattainable luxury
too slowly / and therefore / be bought as a matter of course by ordinary households
explanation: A steep fall in price makes a once-expensive system widely affordable. In each of the other options the result contradicts the rate of change.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: ____ Harel, who holds that every role an actor plays reveals something of the actor's own character, Lavi ____ the actor and the character, because in his view the character ____ . Nevertheless, even Lavi sometimes says things like "In this scene ____ reveals his own fears."
choices: Like / emphasizes the similarity between / has an existence of its own / the character
Unlike / emphasizes the similarity between / has no existence of its own / the actor
Like / prefers to separate / has no existence of its own / the actor
Unlike / insists on a clear distinction between / has an existence of its own / the actor
explanation: Lavi separates actor from character, unlike Harel, yet "nevertheless" slips into attributing the fears to the actor. (2) has him agree with Harel after "unlike"; (1) and (3) mismatch the reason with the position.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: I wanted to know whether the new Thai restaurant in town was worth a visit, and when Ido told me, "It isn't one of the ____ Thai restaurants I've eaten at," I understood that the answer was ____ , since ____ , to the point that ____ .
choices: best / no / Ido has been so impressed by the Thai restaurants he has visited / even an average Thai restaurant is worth trying
worst / yes / Ido dislikes Thai food so strongly / a remark like that from him means the restaurant may well suit my taste
worst / no / Ido has such refined taste in Thai food / even a restaurant he considers acceptable is sure to delight me
best / yes / Ido admires Thai cuisine so greatly / if even he has doubts about the place, that proves its quality
explanation: From someone who dislikes Thai food, "not among the worst" is high praise, so the answer is yes. In (1) and (3) the explanation implies "yes" while the answer is "no"; in (4) doubts are taken as proof of quality.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: If the apartment across town were ____ spacious than mine, with a rent ____ than mine, I ____ move there, since space is ____ important to me than money.
choices: more / higher / would not / less
less / lower / would / more
more / higher / would / less
less / lower / would not / less
explanation: More space at a higher rent is rejected because money matters more to the speaker than space. In each other option the decision contradicts the stated priority.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the slashes separate the blanks.

steps.stem: In Ofer's view, debating other people's plans at meetings is a poor use of time - far poorer than actually trying things out - ____ . We would then learn what works more quickly, and at the very least we would cause no harm, since harsh criticism at a meeting can discourage colleagues, whereas a failed trial run hurts no one.
choices: and even so, he sees no substitute for such debates. He argues that without them it would be hard to judge the quality of other people's ideas

although a certain amount of critical discussion is necessary for good ideas to develop. In his view, if blunt criticism were encouraged, even at the expense of politeness, fewer bad plans would be carried out
and he maintains that if the time spent picking apart other people's plans were spent testing our own ideas instead, the time would be far better used
and for exactly that reason it is easy to understand his warning against hasty trial runs. If only we could avoid poorly planned trials in advance, we could limit the damage they cause
explanation: "We would then" requires a proposal to replace debating with trying, which only (3) makes. (1) and (2) defend criticism, which the next sentence attacks; (4) warns against the trials the paragraph praises.
steps.instructions: Choose the completion that makes the sentence coherent. Insert the phrases in order; the dots separate the blanks.

steps.stem: While ticket prices for most sporting events have stayed the same, ticket prices for the national basketball league ____ sharply in recent seasons. Unlike in the past, when these tickets were ____ , today many fans ____ buy them.
choices: have risen / affordable for almost everyone / can no longer afford to
